title: The Grove Artifact cannot be edited in any way that violates the Sky Core Atlas, and enforcement rests on one reviewer's judgment
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.6 establishes the hierarchy: "The Grove Artifact cannot be edited in any way that violates the Sky Core Atlas or its specifications of the Sky Primitives, or in any way that is otherwise misaligned. The Operational Facilitator must enforce this rule through their review of Artifact Edit Proposals."

The restriction has three tiers of increasing openness. Violating the Core Atlas is a bounded, textual test. Violating its "specifications of the Sky Primitives" is narrower still — the Primitive definitions are concrete. But "or in any way that is otherwise misaligned" is a **general standard**, importing the Atlas's whole alignment vocabulary as a limit on Agent-level amendment. An edit can be Atlas-compliant on its face and still be blocked.

That is the spirit-of-the-rule doctrine applied downward: the Agent's amendment power is bounded not just by the parent's text but by its purpose. It prevents an Agent from legislating itself out of the ecosystem's intent through technically compliant edits.

The weakness is the enforcement clause. A substantive, open-ended limit is enforced by a single role's review, with no independent check named in this section. The strength of the constraint therefore equals the independence of the Operational Facilitator — which, per A.6.1.1.2.2.2.1.2.1.1.1, is specified in the Executor Agent Amatsu's own Artifact rather than in Grove's.
description: Atlas supremacy over Agent Artifacts is asserted as a substantive limit that includes anything 'otherwise misaligned', but the only enforcement named is the Operational Facilitator's review.
